DOC.EP: EC.02.01.01 The hospital manages safety and security risks.. EP 1. The hospital identifies safety and security risks associated with the environment of care. Note: Risks are identified from internal sources such as ongoing monitoring of the environment, results of root cause analyses, results of annual proactive risk assessments of high-risk processes, and from credible external sources such as Sentinel Event Alerts. (See also

DOC.FINDING: The organization did not perform routine assessments of collected data (PI indicators, EC rounds results, ect) to formulate risks assessments.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization should use collected data to formulate a risk assessment. This assessment should be completed annually and used to devise goals and plans for the upcoming year. Additionally, the organization should use the data from this assessment to develop detailed analysis of identified risks (security issues, safety concerns, etc.) The risk assessment format should be used to document these assessments. ? The organization has addressed this concern. EP 3. The hospital takes action to minimize or eliminate identified safety and security risks in the physical environment.
DOC.FINDING: During the building tour of departments, the following was observed: 1. staff not wearing gloved while handling specimens in the lab 2. Fire extinguisher not secured in the Tulsa MCCA office 3. Door stops used to prop open doors in the women’s center clinic 4. Staff on floor no. 4 west did not know the location of the chemo spill kit
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization should address each issue listed. ? The organization has addressed this concern. EP 8. The hospital controls access to and from areas it identifies as security sensitive.
DOC.FINDING: On review of separated/terminated employee information for the past 60 days, the following was revealed: 1. employees were not removed from access to the Pharmacy, ISM (Information System Management) BCMA and CPRS systems 2. Employee badges were not collected on discharge 3. employees were not properly removed from the HR system.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? Based on information and review of separated/terminated employees, the organization has not controlled access to all information systems, clinical systems, and hospital areas. The organization must develop a method to effectively collect and terminate employee access upon termination or discharge. ? The organization has addressed this concern.

DOC.EP: EC.02.03.05 The hospital maintains fire safety equipment and fire safety building features. Note: This standard does not require hospitals to have the types of fire safety equipment and building features described below. However, if these types of equipment or features exist within the building, then the following maintenance, testing, and inspection requirements apply. EP 1. At least quarterly, the hospital tests supervisory signal devices (except valve tamper switches). The completion date of the tests is documented. Note: For additional guidance on performing tests, see NFPA 72, 1999 edition (Table 7-3.2).
DOC.FINDING: During the review of fire component testing records, documentation of quarterly testing for the fire pump supervisory signal was not provided. The organization has not documented testing of the supervisor signal from the fire pump quarterly
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must test and verify operational of supervisory signals at least quarterly. The fire pump supervisory signal must be tested and include "pump running" and "pump failure" signal tests EP 10. For automatic sprinkler systems: Every quarter, the hospital inspects all fire department water supply connections. The completion dates of the inspections are documented. Note: For additional guidance on performing tests, see NFPA 25, 1998 edition (Section 9-7.1).
DOC.FINDING: CBOC Tulsa: quarterly inspection of the FDC (fire department connections) was not completed and documented.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must inspect and document inspection of FDC at least quarterly EP 13. Every 6 months, the hospital inspects any automatic fire- extinguishing systems in a kitchen. The completion dates of the inspections are documented. Note 1: Discharge of the fire-extinguishing systems is not required. Note 2: For additional guidance on performing inspections, see NFPA 96, 1998 edition.
DOC.FINDING: Semi-annual testing of the kitchen hood automatic extinguishing system was not completed and documented. Staff indicated that testing was completed one time during 2010. However, documentation of testing was not provided.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must ensure that al kitchen hood extinguisher devices are tested at least semi-annually EP 15. At least monthly, the hospital inspects portable fire extinguishers. The completion dates of the inspections are documented. Note 1: There are many ways to document the inspections, such as using bar-coding equipment, using check marks on a tag, or using an inventory. Note 2: Inspections involve a visual check for the presence and correct type of extinguisher, broken parts, full charge, and ease of access. Note 3: For additional guidance on inspection of fire extinguishers, see NFPA 10, Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers, 1998 edition (Sections 1-6, 4-3, and 4-4).
DOC.FINDING: Fire extinguishers in the facility were not checked since April 2009. One fire extinguisher was out of date more than one year. Fire extinguisher inspections were not completed at least every 30 days. Inspection tag indicated inconsistencies in testing frequency
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must check each fire extinguisher at least every 30 days. The monthly check must be documented. ? The organization must conduct monthly fire extinguisher testing at frequency not greater than 30 days. EP 19. Every 12 months, the hospital tests automatic smoke-detection shutdown devices for air-handling equipment. The completion date of the tests is documented. Note: For additional guidance on performing tests, see NFPA 90A, Standard for the Installation of Air Conditioning and Ventilation Systems, 1999 edition (Section 4-4.1).
DOC.FINDING: CBOC Tulsa: AHIUs (air handler units) do not shut down on activation of duct detectors
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must provide required HVAC and AHU shut-down devices. AHU's must shut-down on activation of duct detectors.

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.01 The hospital manages risks associated with its utility systems. EP 2. The hospital maintains a written inventory of all operating components of utility systems or maintains a written inventory of selected operating components of utility systems based on risks for infection, occupant needs, and systems critical to patient care (including all life-support systems). The hospital evaluates new types of utility components before initial use to determine whether they should be included in the inventory. (See also EC.02.05.05, EPs 1, 3-5)
DOC.FINDING: Utility components included in the program were not selected based on risk criteria listed in the standard
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? Every utility must be evaluated and included in the program based on risks. The organization must develop a risk criteria based evaluation for evaluation of utility components and need to include in program. ? This remains a concern. EP 4. The hospital identifies, in writing, the intervals for inspecting, testing, and maintaining all operating components of the utility systems on the inventory, based on criteria such as manufacturers' recommendations, risk levels, or hospital experience. (See also

DOC.FINDING: The organization has developed written intervals for inspecting utilities. The intervals are not based on risk levels (See EP 2) and hospital experience
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? Once the hospital completes the risk assessment, intervals for PM (preventative maintenance activates must be developed using manufacturers recommended guides, risk level, and past experience for that utility. The organization must document (in policy) how the frequency for testing was developed.

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.07 The hospital inspects, tests, and maintains medical gas and vacuum systems. Note: This standard does not require hospitals to have the medical gas and vacuum systems discussed below. However, if a hospital has these types of systems, then the following inspection, testing, and maintenance requirements apply. EP 1. At 30-day intervals, the hospital performs a functional test of battery-powered lights required for egress for a minimum duration of 30 seconds. The completion date of the tests is documented.
DOC.FINDING: At 30-day intervals, the hospital performs a functional test of battery-powered lights required for egress for a minimum duration of 30 seconds. The completion date of the tests is documented. The organization has a medical gas and vacuum system policy. However, the policy did not define the testing frequency for components of the program.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? For the 11th street CBOC in Tulsa, the emergency egress lighting was not checked at least monthly for 30 seconds. ? The organization must listed specific testing frequency for each component, including but not limited to: manifold, zone valves, and in-room connection. EP 2. Every 12 months, the hospital either performs a functional test of battery-powered lights required for egress for a duration of 1 1/2 hours; or the hospital replaces all batteries every 12 months and, during replacement, performs a random test of 10% of all batteries for 1 1/2 hours. The completion date of the tests is documented.
DOC.FINDING: For the 11th street CBOC, the emergency egress lighting was not checked at least annually for 90 minutes, or the batteries replaced.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization should test batteries or; replace batteries and test 10% of all replaced batteries. ? The organization has addressed this concern.

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.09 The hospital inspects, tests, and maintains medical gas and vacuum systems. Note: This standard does not require hospitals to have the medical gas and vacuum systems discussed below. However, if a hospital has these types of systems, then the following inspection, testing, and maintenance requirements apply. EP 1. In time frames defined by the hospital, the hospital inspects, tests, and maintains critical components of piped medical gas systems, including master signal panels, area alarms, automatic pressure switches, shutoff valves, flexible connectors, and outlets. These activities are documented. (See also EC.02.05.01, EP 3)
DOC.FINDING: The organization has a medical gas and vacuum system policy. However, the policy did not define the testing frequency for components of the program.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must listed specific testing frequency for each component, including but not limited to: manifold, zone valves, and in-room connection.

DOC.EP: EC.02.06.05 The hospital manages its environment during demolition, renovation, or new construction to reduce risk to those in the organization. EP 3. The hospital takes action based on its assessment to minimize risks during demolition, construction, or renovation.
DOC.FINDING: During review of the OR renovation project, it was revealed that negative air pressure from the entrance was not sufficient. The manometer indicated -0.005 inches water.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? In order to prevent dust exposure during construction activities, the organization must provide adequate negative pressure. Recommended negative pressurization should be maintained between 0.03 and 0.05 inches water.

DOC.EP: EC.04.01.01 The hospital collects information to monitor conditions in the environment. EP 15. Every 12 months, the hospital evaluates each environment of care management plan, including a review of the plan’s objectives, scope, performance, and effectiveness. (See also EC.01.01.01, EPs 3-8;

DOC.FINDING: Review of annual evaluation for environment of care plans revealed that effectives was not consistently evaluated. Effectiveness of the program was documented for only the "medical equipment program".
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must ensure that each plan is evaluated for effectiveness

DOC.EP: EC.04.01.05 The hospital collects information to monitor conditions in the environment. EP 3. The hospital reports performance improvement results to those responsible for analyzing environment of care issues. (See also

DOC.FINDING: The organizations EOC committee and EOC group collect data for performance improvement. However, the data is not reported in the EOC committee at least quarterly or discussed during the year in the committee.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The consultant recommends that the EOC committee discuss PI measures at least quarterly. These measures should be measurable and used to improve identified issues important to the EOC group and leadership. Effectiveness of PI and results of improvement actions must be documented in the committee and on the annual report.
